text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- The finance ministry shortlists Getronics, IBM Nederland and Germany's Daimler-Benz unit Debis as candidates for taking over software firm Roccade. (p1)
- Merger between construction companies BAM and Wilma falls through. (p1)
- Finance ministry is to reopen subscription to its latest 10-year bond on Tuesday.(p1)
- Dutch economy is to get an extra impulse from higher purchasing power because of lower inflation figures. (p1)
- Music and video shops chain Free Record Shop gives profit warning. (p3)
- Automation group Sanderink Beheer buys rival Multihouse that is currently under court protection from creditors following a Dfl 173 million claim. (p3)
- Plastics maker and wholesaler Welna books 30 percent net profit increase in first quarter. (p3)
- Dela, the Netherland's largest funeral insurer aims to boost the number of its policy holders to two million by the end of this year. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- PSV Eindhoven wins the Dutch football league. (p1)
- Economic affairs ministry puts aside two million guilders to clean up pollution at shipping wharf Wilton Fijenoord. (p2)
- Entertainment group Endemol's co-director John de Mol says he is not worried by poor performance of the company's shares. (p4)
- Liberal coalition party VVD is dissatisfied with PM Wim Kok and foreign affairs minister Hans van Mierlo's work at this weekend's EU summit. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Nearly half of the Netherlands population worry about their pensions. (p1)
- New leader of the Christian Democrats Jaap de Hoop Scheffer attacks junior health minister Erica Terpstra for lack of vision on care for the elderly. (p3)
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM's idea to move Schiphol Airport to another location is one of the options being considered for the furture by the airport. (p8)
- Dredger Van Oord sees 1996 net climb from Dfl 12.1 million to Dfl 17.3 million. (p13)
TROUW
- Christian farmers association NCB calls for more preventive slaughtering of pigs to fight swine fever epidemic.
- Christian Democrats CDA seeks to concentrate airline
traffic as long as possible at Schiphol Airport. (p4)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Dutch police have plans to test motorists for drug use (p1)
- Germany's Social Democrats (SPD) says the Dutch economic
success is founded on statistical deception. (p11)
